judgements.reason: untouched: init still writes only the paths installed_files names and never rewrites a file; the amendment only moves the stamp's line-ending wording into the system term, which reads the same (LF or CRLF)
untouched: every changed version rule still only reads and writes to stderr; how a line ending is read decides what is reported, not whether anything is written
untouched: splitting lint's run into reading, the model-version gate and checking adds no write; every outcome is a report, stderr or an exit status

untouched: its findings reach stdout only through lint.run.output after lint.run.model lets the tree be checked, so reading files before the model gate changes nothing observable; it does not depend on carriage returns

findings.text: system.line-ending now defines a line ending as LF or CRLF, with a lone carriage return belonging to the line. Yet lint.findings.line-ending still describes 'a file whose lines end with a carriage return', and lint.layout.line-ending's Then speaks of the [line endings] of <file>, while its Otherwise reports any carriage return, including a lone one inside a line, which by the new term is no line ending at all.
